verdict.rationale: Anytype's local-first architecture, encryption at rest, and local-only mode ('not even Anytype can see your content') mean user data isn't centrally accessible for training purposes, and offline/local-only mode fully removes cloud transmission. However there is no explicit stated policy about AI training use of data, and community evidence notes indexes are not yet encrypted, which is a partial gap in the privacy story. Missing for 10: an explicit anti-AI-training data policy statement, and confirmation that all metadata/indexes (not just content) are protected from any first- or third-party AI training use.
